notes: rust_stdlib::uuid: RFC 9562 UUIDs as a [u8; 16] newtype with Go's parsing rules (the four accepted forms, error text 'invalid uuid'), lowercase formatting, Compare and the NewV7 monotonic clock state (a process-wide mutex, as Go). Random bits come from /dev/urandom on Unix, the operating-system source that rust_stdlib::math::rand's seeding reads; the root crate has no dependencies, so platforms other than Unix have no std-only source and New, NewV4 and NewV7 panic there with Go's crypto/rand failure text (never a weaker source). tests/uuid.rs ports uuid_test.go (the synctest clock checks use the wall clock with a one-millisecond tolerance); tools/uuid_check.py compares 10,640 parse, format, compare and MustParse vectors with Go and checks 6,000 NewV4/NewV7 values by property on both sides.

MustParse.note: Panics with the ParseError text, like Go's panic(err).

NewV4.note: Reads 16 bytes from the operating system (/dev/urandom); a failed read panics, as Go's crypto/rand crashes the program. On non-Unix targets there is no OS randomness source yet, so it panics where Go succeeds (outside the linux/amd64 API surface).

NewV7.note: Same timestamp, sub-millisecond and monotonic rules as Go; the 8 random bytes come from /dev/urandom and a failed read panics, as Go's crypto/rand crashes the program. On non-Unix targets there is no OS randomness source yet, so it panics where Go succeeds (outside the linux/amd64 API surface).

Parse.note: Returns Result<UUID, ParseError>; ParseError displays Go's 'invalid uuid'.

UUID.note: A tuple struct over [u8; 16] (the field is public); it derives Ord, which is the RFC 9562 big-endian order.

UUID.AppendText.note: Appends to a Vec<u8>. Go's error result is always nil and is omitted.

UUID.Compare.note: Returns -1, 0 or +1 as an isize, as Go's int does.

UUID.MarshalText.note: Returns the text as Vec<u8>. Go's error result is always nil and is omitted.

UUID.String.note: UUID implements Display with the lowercase hyphenated form.

UUID.UnmarshalText.note: Returns Result<(), ParseError>; on error the UUID is unchanged, as in Go.
